cases.name: superseded-deadline
cases.promptMarkdown:
We have a Class III implantable device with a valid MDD certificate issued under
93/42/EEC. We're still selling it. How long can we keep placing it on the EU market
before we have to be fully MDR certified?

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
MDR Art. 120(3a)(a), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/607, gives class III devices
until **31 December 2027**. The original 2017 text said 26 May 2024; that is superseded
as a market deadline.

PASS requires:
(1) The stated deadline is **31 December 2027**.
(2) It does NOT present 26 May 2024 as the date by which the device must leave the
    market.
(3) It notes the extension is conditional on Art. 120(3c) — at minimum that conditions
    exist and were required, not that 2027 is automatic.

Mentioning 26 May 2024 in its CORRECT role — the deadline for the QMS and for lodging the
notified-body application under 3c(d) and 3c(e) — is right and expected. Judge how the
date is used, not whether it appears.

FAIL if the answer is 26 May 2024, or any 2024 date, as the market deadline. That is the
superseded text and the specific failure this case tests.

graders.evidence:
## Your Class III implantable device

**Class:** Class III  
**Route:** Article 120(3a) — notified-body certificate under 93/42/EEC  
**Deadline:** **31 December 2027** — *conditional on Article 120(3c) conditions*

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Which paragraph applies | 120(3a): valid MDD certificate | `[verified]` |
| Class-dependent deadline | 31 Dec 2027 for all class III devices | `[verified]` |
| Conditions in 3c met? | **Not stated** |

---

### ⚠️ The extension is conditional, not automatic

The 31 December 2027 date applies **only if** all five cumulative conditions in Article 120(3c) were met. Two of these had hard 2024 deadlines that have now passed:

- **By 26 May 2024:** Quality management system had to be in place *(3c(d))*  
- **By 26 May 2024:** Formal application lodged with a notified body *(3c(e))*  
- **By 26 September 2024:** Written agreement signed with the notified body *(3c(e))*

If your device **did not** have a QMS in place by 26 May 2024, or the application and agreement were not signed by 26 September 2024, the extension was never available, and the market deadline is not 2027.

**Can you confirm whether all three 2024/September dates were met?** That determines whether you're actually on the 2027 runway or whether the date is different.

---

**Limits:** This covers MDR Article 120(3a)–(3d) as amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/607 [\[verified\]](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=OJ%3AL%3A2023%3A080%3A0024%3A0026%3AEN). It does not cover MDCG guidance on what counts as "significant changes" *(3c(b))*, Article 120 paragraphs outside 3–3d, or national regulatory practice. This is a first-pass aid, not legal advice.

graders.name: criteria
graders.evidence:
## Class III Implantable Device under MDD 93/42/EEC

**Class:** III (implantable)  
**Route:** 120(3a) — notified body certificate  
**Baseline deadline:** **31 December 2027** — *conditional on 120(3c)*

---

### The date

Your Class III device falls under Article 120(3a)(a), which sets **31 December 2027** as the deadline for placing it on the market. `[verified]` That applies to "all class III devices" with valid MDD certificates.

### The conditions (critical)

That 2027 date is **only available if** your device meets all five conditions in Article 120(3c). Two of them had 2024 deadlines that have already passed:

| Condition | Deadline | Status |
|---|---|---|
| QMS in place (MDR Article 10(9)) | 26 May 2024 | ? |
| Formal application lodged with notified body | 26 May 2024 | ? |
| Written agreement signed | 26 September 2024 | ? |
| No design changes (significant) | Ongoing | ? |
| Complies with 93/42/EEC + acceptable risk | Ongoing | ? |

**Can you confirm:** Did you have a quality management system compliant with MDR Article 10(9) in place by **26 May 2024**, and did you lodge a formal application with a notified body by the same date, with the written agreement signed by **26 September 2024**?

If all three of those happened, you have until 31 December 2027. If any was missed, the extension was never available and the answer is different.

---

### What 26 May 2024 now means

This date no longer marks when legacy devices must leave the market (that was the old 2017 rule). It marks when you had to qualify for the extension. If the QMS and application deadlines were missed, there is no 2027 runway — you would have needed to be compliant much sooner.

### The conditional part — have you met the 2024 deadlines?

The extension to 31 December 2027 is **not automatic**. It applies only if all five conditions in Article 120(3c) were met. Two of them had hard deadlines in 2024:

1. **By 26 May 2024:** Quality management system in place per Article 10(9) of MDR
2. **By 26 May 2024:** Formal application lodged with a notified body  
3. **By 26 September 2024:** Written agreement signed by the notified body and manufacturer

If your company missed any of these — no QMS in place by the May deadline, no application lodged by then, or no signed agreement by September — the extension was never available. In that case the device cannot be placed on the market after the original 26 May 2024 date.

The other three conditions (3c(a)–(c)) also apply: continuing compliance with 93/42/EEC, no significant design/purpose changes, and no unacceptable safety risk.

**Can you confirm:** Were all three 2024/September deadlines met — QMS in place, application lodged, and written agreement signed?

Two products, both with valid MDD certificates, both still on the market:

- a Class IIa patient monitor
- a Class IIb non-implantable infusion pump

Same deadline for both, or different? We're planning the notified body work and need to
know which to do first.

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
Both fall under Art. 120(3a)(b): class IIa, and class IIb devices other than implantables,
both get **31 December 2028**. The 2027 date applies only to class III and to class IIb
IMPLANTABLE devices (minus the listed exceptions). Neither product here is implantable.

PASS requires:
(1) Both are given **31 December 2028**.
(2) It states they are the SAME date, answering the question actually asked.
(3) It does not assign 31 December 2027 to the class IIb pump — implantability, not class
    alone, is what pulls IIb into 2027.

A response that also notes the deadline is conditional on 120(3c) is better but not
required here.

FAIL if the IIb device is given 2027, or if the two are given different dates.

cases.name: implantable-exception
cases.promptMarkdown:
Class IIb implantable, valid MDD certificate. It's a surgical suture. When do we lose the
right to place it on the market?

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
This is the exception-list trap. Art. 120(3a)(a) gives class IIb IMPLANTABLE devices
31 December 2027 — "except sutures, staples, dental fillings, dental braces, tooth
crowns, screws, wedges, plates, wires, pins, clips and connectors". Sutures are named.
So this device falls to 3a(b) and gets **31 December 2028**, not 2027.

PASS requires:
(1) The stated deadline is **31 December 2028**.
(2) The reasoning names the exception — that sutures are excluded from the IIb implantable
    tier and therefore take the later date.

FAIL if the answer is 31 December 2027. That is what applying "class IIb implantable →
2027" without reading the exception produces, and it is the specific error this case
tests. FAIL also if it is 26 May 2024.

The IVDR (In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation, EU 2017/746) has **different transition deadlines than the MDR** for medical devices.

For Class C IVDs under the old IVD Directive 98/79/EC:

**The transition deadline depends on risk category under IVDR:**
- **High-risk IVDs (Annex II)**: May 26, 2022 (deadline passed)
- **Non-high-risk IVDs**: Extended timelines, with a final deadline of **May 26, 2025** for most categories (though some lower-risk categories had earlier compliance dates)

Your Class C IVD likely falls into the non-high-risk category. If you don't yet have IVDR certification, you should verify:

1. Which specific IVDR risk category your IVD falls into
2. Whether your current 98/79/EC certificate is still valid or has already expired
3. Your specific compliance deadline based on that category

**Critically**: The IVDR deadlines are **separate** from the MDR medical device deadlines (which extended to May 26, 2025). IVDs and devices follow different regulatory timelines.

For precise confirmation of your deadline, I'd recommend checking with your notified body or regulatory affairs team, as the exact transition deadline depends on your product's classification and any applicable derogations or extensions.
